calls.reason: The packet's temporal studies do not connect reasoning performance to world-model presence, and it supplies no corresponding inflation or price evidence. The necessity claim remains unclear.

Karvonen's chess study finds learned board-state representations and validates them through interventions. That directly challenges the central assertion that language models never learn usable world models, although broader error causes remain unresolved.

The packet lacks the original task record or an analysis of what caused GPT-5's errors. Gurnee and Tegmark's findings concern other models and cannot distinguish historical-knowledge failures from filtering or enumeration failures here.
This is an open-ended, rhetorical judgment about future learning. The packet's temporal benchmark does not pair chess failures with everyday reasoning results for the same system.

Tom's Guide's August 2025 SimpleBench report places every tested model below the 83.7% human baseline on ordinary-knowledge reasoning challenges. This supports recurring commonsense failures, although it does not measure everyday usage rates.

RuleArena documents failures with supplied rules, while Fauber's specialized chess model nearly always proposes legal moves. These mixed results do not establish whether LLMs lack abstract models they can reliably use.
